assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window on the universe: IceCube detected a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos, then evidence for TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. This is a large detector instrument concept executed in Antarctic ice, with clear originality and lasting impact on multi-messenger astronomy. As an experimentalist in astroparticle physics I weigh the instrumental achievement heavily.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and the high-energy neutrino-astronomy programme; Spiering is credited for the long pioneering path from DUMAND and Baikal to the IceCube-era science. The supplied credit supports a two-person prize, though a large collaboration and other early pioneers make the allocation sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux is established by independent analyses; source identification is still partial and the TXS and Galactic-plane results are a few years old. Recognition is timely but could be argued as slightly early for source astronomy; the detector and discovery of the flux are mature.
uncertainties: Whether the individual attributions to Halzen and Spiering fully capture the decisive contributions among the founders of neutrino telescopes.
Source associations beyond one blazar and the Galactic plane remain statistically modest, and I am relying on my recollection rather than verifying details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 1e-18 level transformed time and frequency metrology, based on Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability. They open tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. Originality and impact are high, and the physics is clean.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock; Ye led the realisation of record performance with strontium and the associated frequency-comb and spectroscopy work. The two names are a natural pairing, although Hall and Hansch were already honoured for combs and other clock developers contributed to ion clocks.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm 1e-18 operation and clock comparisons; the redefinition of the second is under discussion but not yet done. Timing is good with strong, stable confirmation.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior recognition of frequency combs and ion-clock work may affect how the Committee frames the contribution.
Relative weight of Katori's proposal versus Ye's performance records is a matter of judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping and precision spectroscopy of antimatter test CPT and matter-antimatter symmetry at extraordinary precision: antihydrogen trapping and 1S-2S and hyperfine measurements, and single-particle antiproton and positron magnetic-moment work. Beyond cold-trap technique, this is experimental craft I appreciate, given my own antimatter-in-cosmic-rays experience with PAMELA, though that is a different regime.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse led antiproton and positron trapping, and the electron g-factor and antihydrogen efforts of ATRAP; Hangst led ALPHA, which first trapped antihydrogen and performed spectroscopy. The supplied two-name credit leaves out other ALPHA and ATHENA leaders such as Fujiwara and the broader ALPHA team, so allocation is not straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Results are confirmed by independent collaborations at the CERN Antiproton Decelerator, and the precision keeps improving. No violation of CPT has been seen, so the prize would reward technique and precision rather than a surprising finding; this is a mature but still evolving field.
uncertainties: Competition and priority between ATHENA, ATRAP and ALPHA and the many contributors to the antihydrogen programme.
Null results to date may make the Committee prefer to wait for a discrepancy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with its flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity launched twistronics and moire quantum matter, an original and field-defining discovery with a rapidly expanding body of work. The combination of a theoretical prediction and a clean experimental demonstration is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat band; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated and superconducting states. This gives a theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Cao and Fatemi in the experiment and other theorists such as Santos and Peres or Lopes dos Santos might be considered.
assessment.maturity: Many groups reproduced the phenomena, and the field is mature in confirming existence, yet interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and many-body states remains unsettled, so recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Interpretation of superconductivity and the correlated states is not settled.
Credit among early theorists and student experimentalists is delicate and I cannot verify all priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created the architecture for superconducting quantum processors and the strong-coupling regime for microwave photons with artificial atoms; the impact on quantum technology and precise control of quantum systems is major. Needs consideration against recent recognition of macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf (with Wallraff, not among the supplied names) proposed and demonstrated circuit QED; the supplied credit supports a three-person prize, although Wallraff's experiment was decisive and cannot be included from this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted across the field, with independent confirmations by many groups; technological maturity high. The recent related prize makes timing delicate.
uncertainties: Absence of Andreas Wallraff from the supplied credit weakens attribution.
Possible perceived overlap with the most recent superconducting-circuits recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for quantum-enhanced interferometry underpins improved sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors and connects quantum optics to precision measurement; the concept is original and the practical impact is clear. As an instrumentalist, I value the demonstrated gain in real detectors.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the theory of squeezing in interferometers, Kimble the first experimental squeezed light generation, and Schnabel the long-term squeezed-light implementation in GEO600 and LIGO. Mavalvala and others (Slusher, Wu) also contributed so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is routine in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600, so it is mature; the Nobel in 2017 already recognised the detectors, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Selecting three names from a larger group, including Slusher and Wu, is difficult and I cannot verify priority claims.
Overlap with the 2017 prize for LIGO.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and later the framework of quantum simulation with cold atoms, concepts that shaped experimental quantum information science. Originality is very high and the lasting influence spans two platforms.
assessment.attribution: The two are tightly paired and their proposals are widely recognised as foundational; the supplied credit is compact and fair. Experimental realisation credit goes to others (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe), which is partly recognised already.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation of the proposals is extensive, but the broader quantum-computing outcome is still unfolding; the Committee might prefer to recognise theory together with experiment.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers theory proposals without experimental co-recipients.
Overlap with prior Wineland recognition and with other quantum-simulation candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and rests on exceptional detector design and collaboration; as an experimentalist with CERN background I value the instrumentation achievement. The theory was already recognised in 2013.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributors are large collaborations; a three-person limit cannot capture all founders and spokespersons, and the set of four credited names is cut to three. Choosing Jenni and Della Negra as founding proponents with Gianotti as spokesperson at discovery is a judgement, with Virdee as an equally strong alternative.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed extensively by independent measurements in two experiments; the discovery is mature but the prize rules and the 2013 award mean the experimental recognition depends on the Committee's views on collaborations.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among ATLAS and CMS leaders and exclusion of Virdee.
Whether the Committee considers the experimental recognition already covered by the 2013 prize.
